title: Power Level Monitor
description: Monitor ship power levels using WHILE loop until power reaches safe threshold.

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "The ship's power is recharging, but we need to wait until it hits at least 75% before we can restart systems. Let's monitor it with a WHILE loop."
story.context: In real automation, you often wait for a condition to be met. WHILE loops are perfect for polling—repeatedly checking a value until it meets your criteria.
story.success: MENTOR-9: "Good! The power reached 75% and the loop stopped. In real tests, you'd be checking actual system status instead of incrementing a variable, but the pattern is the same."

instructions: After loop, log 'Power sufficient! Systems can restart.'
hints: Condition checks if power is LESS than 75
Loop will stop when power reaches 75 or higher
solution:
*** Test Cases ***
Monitor Power Levels
    ${power}=    Set Variable    50
    WHILE    ${power} < 75
        Log    Power at ${power}%
        ${power}=    Set Variable    ${power + 5}
    END
    Log    Power sufficient! Systems can restart.

theory.title: Exercise 3.1.2: Monitoring with WHILE Loops
theory.content:
MENTOR-9 shows you the power gauge slowly climbing.

"We can't control how fast it charges, but we CAN wait until it's safe. This is a classic polling pattern—check, wait, check again, until the condition is met."

Polling Pattern

Polling means repeatedly checking a value until it meets a condition. Common in automation:

  • Waiting for page to load
  • Monitoring system status
  • Checking file existence
  • Waiting for process completion

Basic Pattern:

WHILE    ${current_value} != ${target_value}
    ${current_value}=    Get Current Status
    Sleep    1s  # Wait before checking again
END
